(1) unsupervised learning is useful for classification, (2) the combination of different unsupervised learning techniques can improve the performance of the classifier, and (3) the use of transfer learning is a very effective way to improve performance.

the best way to learn a good representation for a given task is (1) to use a large set of labeled and unlabeled data, (2) to use a deep learning architecture, (3) to use a good initialization, (4) to use a transfer strategy, and (5) to combine different kinds of layers, each of them being adapted to a specific task.

the question of how to learn representations of data in a deep way, and in particular, how to learn such representations from unlabeled data.

the challenge was won with a deep learning approach.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we used deep architectures to learn a good representation of the data in the unsupervised setting, and then we used this representation to solve the supervised classification problem.

we have developed a simple and effective approach for learning good representations in the unsupervised and transfer learning setting, and for using these representations to improve the performance of a simple classifier.

the challenge has shown the interest of a multi-layer approach to transfer learning, where each layer is a different unsupervised learning algorithm, and that a linear classifier trained on a small number of labeled samples can be competitive with state-of-the art classifiers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple combination of unsupervised algorithms can outperform more sophisticated approaches, when the goal is to learn representations that are transferable across datasets.
the combination of several unsupervised algorithms is a powerful way to extract good representations.

it is possible to learn good representations in the unsupervised learning setting with a small set of labeled data, and that the best way to combine different kinds of representations depends on the particular dataset.
